App Store Connect field limits — zh-Hans listing reference

Apple publishes per-field character caps in App Store Connect. The table below reflects Apple's documented limits as operator guidance for Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) listings. Apple may change caps — always verify the live counter in Connect for your locale row before you save.

Connect field Typical cap Visible in Search? What overflows look like
App name (title) ~30 characters Yes — primary Search line Truncated mid-phrase in results; brand plus category noun does not fit
Subtitle ~30 characters Yes — under app name in Search English-style feature stack (“Track · Plan · Focus”) translated to 40+ chars
Keywords (hidden) ~100 characters No — indexing only Comma list from ChatGPT repeats title nouns and exceeds 100 chars
Promotional text ~170 characters Yes — above description on product page Seasonal promo translated literally from a 120-word English paragraph
Description Up to ~4,000 characters Partial — first lines skimmed Less often hard-rejected; still suffers from 翻译腔 and keyword stuffing
What's New (release notes) Up to ~4,000 characters On version history English bullet list pasted through a model without per-line counting

Field-specific guides: app name (~30 chars), subtitle (~30 chars), keywords (~100 chars), promotional text (~170 chars).

Why CJK overflows when English fits

Western teams often budget listing copy in English words or rough letter counts. App Store Connect counts characters per locale — and Chinese morphemes carry more meaning per visible glyph than English letters do per word.

  • Not word-for-word — “Focus timer for deep work” is six English words (~28 chars). A faithful zh-Hans rewrite might be 专注计时·深度工作模式 — fewer glyphs than a literal translation, but still a rewrite job, not a paste.
  • Literal translation expands — “The ultimate productivity companion for busy professionals” translates to formal brochure Chinese that routinely exceeds 30 characters in both title and subtitle slots.
  • One concept, multiple characters — English acronyms and coined brands (PDF, AI, SaaS) become multi-character Chinese phrases or explanatory nouns Chinese users actually search.
  • Punctuation counts — middle dots (·), full-width commas，and em dashes consume the same budget as Han characters in Connect's counter.
  • Traditional vs Simplified — zh-Hant (Taiwan, Hong Kong) shares similar caps but different morpheme choices; OpenCC conversion does not shrink character count to fit.

Pomodoro focus & task lists — 28 characters ✓

番茄钟专注计时与任务清单管理工具 — 14 characters shown; full string often 16–18 Han chars but models add filler → overflow

Counted AppLocale rewrite (29 chars):

Overflow example — keywords (~100 characters)

ChatGPT often returns a keyword paragraph that repeats title nouns:

番茄钟,专注,待办,习惯,效率,时间管理,任务管理,清单,提醒,深度工作,专注模式,学习,考研,自律 — frequently 110–130+ characters ✗

Counted pack within ~100 characters removes duplicates already visible in title/subtitle and keeps searchable synonyms.

Overflow example — promotional text (~170 characters)

A two-sentence English promo (142 chars) becomes 200+ Chinese characters when the model preserves every English clause. Connect may accept description-length overflow in promo less often than you'd expect — and truncated promo text mid-offer reads broken on the product page.

DIY ChatGPT failure mode

The typical workflow: copy en-US fields → paste into ChatGPT with “translate to Simplified Chinese for App Store” → paste replies into Connect. The model optimizes for fluent paragraphs, not per-field caps.

  • No live counter — ChatGPT does not read your Connect locale row or Apple's current cap for each field
  • Same nouns everywhere — models repeat “效率”, “专注”, “待办” across title, subtitle, description, and keywords — wasting caps and reading as spam
  • Discover overflow at Save — you only learn a field is over limit when Connect flags it or Search shows a truncated title
  • Iterative prompt tuning burns time — “make it shorter” rounds rarely produce idiomatic Chinese that still converts

AppLocale FAQ

What are the App Store Connect character limits for Simplified Chinese?

Apple documents per-field caps in App Store Connect. Operator guidance for zh-Hans listings: app name and subtitle are commonly around 30 characters each; the hidden keyword field around 100 characters; promotional text around 170 characters; description up to around 4,000 characters. Limits can change — verify the live counter in Connect before you save.

Why does Chinese overflow when my English listing fits?

CJK is not 1:1 with English. One English word may become two or three Chinese morphemes. A 28-character English title can become 38 Chinese characters when translated literally. Connect counts characters, not words or bytes — so a draft that looks short in English often exceeds zh-Hans caps.

Does ChatGPT respect App Store Connect character limits for Chinese?

No. ChatGPT and Google Translate output prose without a live Connect counter tied to your locale row. Models routinely deliver zh-Hans titles, subtitles, and keyword strings that exceed Apple's documented caps — you discover overflow only when Connect rejects the save or truncates visible text in Search.
